analysis:
Examined both CI source excerpts, build-documentation metadata and patch against the indexed threat model and supplied T-041 detail. .github/workflows/ci.yml:43-47 replaces one five-job provider lane with five single-job lanes; :143 selects the corresponding route using the fixed shard matrix at :149. docs/developer/build.md:239-246,259-262 documents the same whole-lane allocation contract. Sandbox execution already existed in BASE; this does not independently establish a new untrusted-runner boundary or weakened isolation.
The supplied workflow retains read-only contents permissions (:9-10), a permissionless routing job (:34-38), pinned actions, test prerequisite checks, shard-count auditing (:371-377), and the fail-closed Provider Tests result gate (:770-790). Release/signing publication is not added to these jobs, and cache-swift remains on its literal runner (:792-795). No changed provider authorization, attestation, encryption, billing, prompt handling or production prefix-cache control is visible; T-041 and A-001 mitigations are not modified by the shown cache-disable test settings.
Integration should verify .github/workflows/darkbloom-route.yml and its allocator/tests accept and return all five new keys, enforce single-job grants independently, and preserve the existing runner isolation and fallback contract. Their implementation is outside this supplied scope; documentation is not proof of enforcement. This is a routing/availability uncertainty, not evidence of a regression. Relevant contracts include A-018 and the integrity of test evidence supporting A-017/T-054; no deployment or qualification conclusion is established.
